_comment: STING sheet discipline vocabulary — how a sheet's discipline is decided, and
what that discipline means downstream.
This is the CORPORATE BASELINE. A project overrides it by dropping a file named
sheet_disciplines.json into its _BIM_COORD folder; project entries win by key.
Run 'Reload Disciplines' (Drawing Types -> Title Block) to pick up an edit
without restarting Revit.
numberPrefixes  the letters before the first digit or separator in a sheet
number. 'AR-101' -> AR -> A. This is the strongest signal
there is, because a sheet number is chosen deliberately.
titleKeywords   WHOLE WORDS in the sheet title, tested IN ORDER. Order is part
of the rule: 'COORDINATED SERVICES PLAN' names two things, and
the first rule that matches decides. Declaring any rules here
REPLACES the list rather than appending to it, because rules
appended after the shipped ones could never be reached.
csvColumns      which TITLE_BLOCK.csv column fills a sheet of this discipline.
A discipline with no column gets GEN, the project-wide defaults.
roleLetters     this discipline's ISO 19650 ROLE letter, for the role segment of
the document identifier. The letters themselves are the
standard's, not yours: a value outside ABCDEFGHIKLMPQSTWXYZ is
REJECTED and named in the reload report, because an invalid role
letter looks perfectly ordinary printed on a title block.
